author: Javier Martín
title: Why is it important that the Tesla Roadster uses Optimus's actuators?
subtitle: The cross-pollination between Tesla and SpaceX has once again become evident with the presentation of the Tesla Roadster, and this is also related to the Optimus robot.
body_markdown:
Last week will be remembered for the presentation of **Tesla**'s new **Roadster** model, a car that has gone around the world through the media, just as its predecessor has gone around the solar system after being launched on a **SpaceX** rocket.

That first crazy idea of Elon Musk's, deciding to launch a car into space as a kind of tribute to what this vehicle had meant for the company, has now been surpassed by making the new version of the car fly; although for now it is over short distances and it seems rather to jump like Knight Rider's car, what the car will be able to do in the future is hard to guess.

But what is not hard to sense is that this car means much more than the launch of a new product, because what it rather seems is the confirmation of the **definitive alliance between Tesla and SpaceX**.

The car's presentation event itself was held at SpaceX's facilities, and everything related to the propulsion that allows the car to fly comes from rockets, but what I wanted to talk about today is **Optimus**, which also took part, albeit discreetly, in this event.

Specifically, Optimus's contribution to the event consisted of lending part of its technology, namely the **actuators** that allow it to move its limbs, but in this case to move the vehicle's rear **spoiler**.

In this way the Tesla Roadster's spoilers use an actuator system developed for the Tesla Optimus robot, which activate Track Mode, allowing it to achieve advanced aerodynamics generating downforce close to that of Formula 1 cars.

So we are facing yet another example of the **cross-pollination** that exists between Tesla and SpaceX in terms of working together, but in this case not just by sharing knowledge but directly through the components that make up their products.

This cross-pollination undoubtedly has many more examples, for example in solar panels, in AI models, even in the next-generation chips they are going to build jointly through [Terafab](https://terafab.ai/).

And why is all this I'm telling you important? Basically because the chances of a merger between Tesla and SpaceX are getting higher and higher, and this could have very important consequences for the future of the Optimus robot.

Let's think, for example, about what happened with the merger of xAI and SpaceX prior to the IPO, where the great expectation generated by the possibility of creating datacenters in space facilitated unprecedented fundraising, which now makes it much easier for SpaceX to develop its plans.

Likewise, with the presentation of the flying Tesla Roadster and this new staging of the collaboration between Tesla and SpaceX, what is becoming evident is that there is no limit to the company's possibilities and capabilities for developing technology and bringing it to market.

It is true that the deadlines Musk sets are never met and that the estimates are very exaggerated, but the reality is indisputable, for example regarding the capacity to put payload into space and create the world's largest satellite communications network.

But let's go back to Optimus, which after all is what interests us most at Integrarobot, and take the opportunity to give an update on its state of development.

![Image](https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/df150e5c-fc74-4a0e-9bcc-1cd3348576a6_2048x1282.png)

Because now that it is time for Tesla to report its results, and it has filed its report for the shareholders' meeting with the [SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000110465926116700/tm267596-1_def14a.htm), more data can be learned that is very useful for knowing the state of development of Optimus. Specifically, this is what the report says:

1. Version 3 of Optimus ready for **mass production** is one of the 4 milestones highlighted in the infographic with which the report opens, together with more than 10 million vehicles delivered, more than 130 GWh of storage deployed and vision-only Robotaxi in the US.
2. Among the infrastructure investments for 2026, the construction of the **first Optimus production lines** is mentioned. It is mentioned in the same sentence as the Semi factory in Nevada and the new data centre capacity to train its Superintelligence systems.
3. Among the decisions Tesla attributes to its governance structure is applying what it has learned in autonomous driving to robots, and it gives Optimus as an example, defining it as an **autonomous general-purpose humanoid robot**.
4. Within the transition from a hardware-focused business to a Physical Superintelligence company, the refinement of the production-ready Optimus design is mentioned, grouped with the advances in FSD, the launch of Robotaxi and the expansion of training infrastructure.

Nothing more and nothing less. That is, we still know very little about Optimus 3, but my conclusion is that the company is no longer interested in demonstrating the robot's great capabilities, but in showing that it is able to mass-produce it, because that is really what the market needs.

## What Cathie Wood thinks about the future of Optimus

Coinciding with the publication of Tesla's status report, the investment management firm [ARK](https://www.ark-invest.com/articles/valuation-models/arks-expected-share-price-for-tesla-2031), led by **Cathie Wood**, has taken the opportunity to reformulate its valuation of the company, setting out several scenarios and including Optimus in the formula that allows it to say that in 2031 a Tesla share could be worth 4,400 dollars.

> "*We believe Optimus Robot-as-a-Service (RaaS) will likely experience an inflection point as robotaxis continue to proliferate, as shown below*".

Specifically, the calculation model ARK has just published indicates that Optimus could contribute 2.29 trillion dollars to Tesla's business in 2031, which would represent 14% of the enterprise value estimated for the company.

To arrive at that figure it calculates one million robots sold cumulatively to other companies and annual revenue of 212 billion dollars. The key is that Tesla could charge a **subscription** for the work of those robots, so that each installed Optimus would become a source of recurring revenue that could grow as its capabilities improved.

Of course, we are talking about a forecast that depends on Tesla managing to manufacture those robots, making them work with enough autonomy and reliability and convincing companies that they are worth paying for.

In addition, it is considered that increasing computing capacity will allow Optimus to approach human performance around 2031, but that relationship still has to be demonstrated in the robot itself.

Impressive figures and incredible estimates, but what ARK says nothing about is whether we will soon see Optimus building habitats for astronauts on Mars, which is what really interests me.

items.headline: 🏭 Siemens shows with NVIDIA how to use AI agents to reorganize production at its Erlangen factory.
items.body_markdown: 🏭 [Siemens](https://blogs.nvidia.com/gtc-berlin-2026-news/?ncid=so-twit-482445#entry-postlet-siemens-and-nvidia-put-industrial-ai-to-work-in-erlangen) shows with **NVIDIA** how to use AI agents to reorganize production at its Erlangen factory. The agents compare materials, capacity and lead times; the changes are tested in a **digital twin**, and a manager approves the plan before it is applied.

items.headline: 🦾 Schaeffler opens a factory in Taicang where, according to the company, six humanoids work at five stations assembling joint modules for other humanoids.
items.body_markdown: 🦾 [Schaeffler](https://www.schaeffler.de/en/news_media/press_releases/press_releases_detail.jsp?id=88222851) opens a factory in Taicang where, according to the company, six humanoids work at five stations assembling **joint modules** for other humanoids. The facility brings together manufacturing, training, data and digital twins.

items.headline: 🚜 AGCO signs an agreement with Agility Robotics to test Digit at its agricultural machinery factory in Hesston, Kansas.
items.body_markdown: 🚜 [AGCO](https://www.agilityrobotics.com/content/agco-and-agility-robotics-advance-smart-manufacturing-with-humanoid-robot-pilot-in-hesston-kansas-facility) signs an agreement with **Agility Robotics** to test Digit at its agricultural machinery factory in Hesston, Kansas. The pilot is planned for 2027 and will begin with sorting and stacking parts and placing containers.

items.headline: 💰 Eka Robotics announces a 150 million dollar Series A led by a16z and F-Prime.
items.body_markdown: 💰 [Eka Robotics](https://ekarobotics.com/blog/eka-robotics-raises-150m-to-build-superhuman-intelligence-for-the-physical-world) announces a **150 million dollar** Series A led by a16z and F-Prime. Its vision, force and action model combines simulation and reinforcement learning to improve manipulation; the company reports up to 1,500 operations per hour in its tests.

items.headline: 🔋 Agility Robotics chooses Nyobolt for Digit 5's battery and announces 90 minutes of operation for every nine of recharging, with the goal of exceeding 20 hours of work a day.
items.body_markdown: 🔋 [Agility Robotics](https://www.agilityrobotics.com/content/agility-robotics-selects-nyobolt-as-its-ultra-fast-charging-battery-technology-partner-for-digit-5) chooses Nyobolt for Digit 5's **battery** and announces 90 minutes of operation for every nine of recharging, with the goal of exceeding 20 hours of work a day. Initial access is expected in the first half of 2027.

items.headline: 🛠️ ASPIRE uses coding agents to write robotic control programs, examine execution failures and save validated corrections as reusable skills.
items.body_markdown: 🛠️ [ASPIRE](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/gear/aspire/) uses coding agents to write robotic control programs, examine execution failures and save validated corrections as **reusable skills**. The NVIDIA project shows tests in simulation and on real robots.

items.headline: 🔎 RAX proposes that an agent learn by exploring with the robot and turn what it discovers into verifiable programs, without human demonstrations or training a policy for the tas…
items.body_markdown: 🔎 [RAX](https://robot-agent-exploration.com/) proposes that an agent learn by exploring with the robot and turn what it discovers into **verifiable programs**, without human demonstrations or training a policy for the tasks studied. The project publishes code, skills and logs of real sessions.

items.headline: 🏷️ Flora brings together open NVIDIA models for describing actions in video and generating labels on the progress and outcome of robotic tasks.
items.body_markdown: 🏷️ [Flora](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/gear/flora/) brings together open **NVIDIA** models for describing actions in video and generating labels on the progress and outcome of robotic tasks. The company states that its system, used to train GR00T, labels **200,000 hours** of data a day with 512 GB300 GPUs.

items.headline: 👷 General Intelligence Labs explains how to turn everyday work into data for robotics through its EGO1 and EGO1GS devices and a processing and review service.
items.body_markdown: 👷 [General Intelligence Labs](https://www.gilabs.xyz/blog/everyday-work-to-robotics-training-data) explains how to turn everyday work into **data for robotics** through its EGO1 and EGO1GS devices and a processing and review service. The system combines recordings from the worker's perspective with motion and depth reconstruction.

items.headline: ⚙️ 120ft presents Factory OS, a proposal for connecting AI models, robots and automation platforms through agents, assembly trees and physical simulation.
items.body_markdown: ⚙️ [120ft](https://120ft.com/technology) presents **Factory OS**, a proposal for connecting AI models, robots and automation platforms through agents, assembly trees and physical simulation. The company proposes reducing programming effort so that automating small orders becomes viable.

items.headline: 🧬 OpenAI acquires Orchestra Bio to combine its drug development coordination platform with the Rosalind models and tools.
items.body_markdown: 🧬 [OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/openai-to-acquire-orchestra-bio/) acquires **Orchestra Bio** to combine its drug development coordination platform with the Rosalind models and tools. It seeks to help teams connect scientific results, studies, decisions and next steps.

items.headline: 🧠 NEURA Robotics presents Neuron AI, a model that integrates 3D vision, touch, force, sound, robot state and language with memory.
items.body_markdown: 🧠 [NEURA Robotics](https://neura-robotics.com/neura-robotics-introduces-neuron-ai/) presents **Neuron AI**, a model that integrates 3D vision, touch, force, sound, robot state and language with memory. According to the company, it works on five types of robots in its catalogue and allows skills to be distributed through Neuraverse. In addition, [NEURA Robotics](https://neura-robotics.com/neura-robotics-nxai-memory-for-physical-ai/) partners with NXAI, Sepp Hochreiter's company, to develop robotic memory based on the recurrent xLSTM architecture. They also plan to incorporate an NXAI model into Neuraverse.
